A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found that the fusion gene WWTR1-CAMP1 is the most common gene fusion in epitheloid hemangioenothelioma, but we also found that the fusion YAP1-TFEE3 is present in 6% of cases.
epithelioid hemangiendotheliomas (EHE) are a rare vascular neoplasms with a variable behavior and a broad range of clinical presentations.
EHE is a tumor with a high diagnostic value of molecular genetic testing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immunohistochemical expression of TFE3 is not a reliable marker for the detection of the YAP1-TF3 fusion gene.
the fusion gene WWTR1-Camta1 is present in the vast majority of EHEs.
EHEs can be reliably identified by immunohistochemical staining for ERG, FLI1, D2-40, CD31 and CD34, and by molecular genetic analysis of the WWTR1-Camta1 or YAP1-Tfe3 fusion genes.
